questions.knowledge_point: Identifying the Intervals on Which a Function is Invertible Given Its Graph
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938271/assets/279c3cd6084423d913186f4ba467ea50d0f794cf54773785777cb8841f5c2ca1.png)

On which of the following intervals is the function $f(x)$ (shown above) invertible?

- $x\in (-3,-1]$
- $x\in [-1,3]$
- $x\in [0,1]$
questions.worked_solution:
A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test. 

- The given function is invertible on the intervals $x\in (-3,-1]$ and on $x\in [0,1].$  Indeed, a horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938271/assets/0388335095ed530ce07d278f82be5eb3bff14859db64b6e9ec47da27861bb657.png)

    

- The given function is **not** invertible on the interval. $x\in [-1,3]$  because some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938271/assets/522b5661aaf9b7640c305b8cefd06f49cc8eed590f3ae736fc6720e6165bc3a9.png)

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only".

questions.problem:
Given that $f(x)=1-x,$ on which of the following intervals is $f(x)$ invertible?

- $x\in (-\infty ,\infty )$
- $x\in (0,\infty )$
- $x\in (-2,2)$
questions.worked_solution:
The function $f(x)$ is a linear function with slope $-1$ and $y$-intercept $1,$ as shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938271/assets/73d9277c040ae457ba6d96e162574edbeeef965d181fa6011ca4ab0e4644bd82.png)

A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.

- The given function is invertible on the interval $x\in (-\infty ,\infty ).$ On this interval, a horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

- Since the function is invertible on $x\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ it is also invertible on $x\in (0,\infty )$ and $x\in (-2,2).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I, II, and III".

questions.problem:
Given that $f(x)=(x-1)^{2}-2,$ on which of the following intervals is $f(x)$ invertible?

- $x\in (-\infty ,1]$
- $x\in (1,\infty )$
- $x\in (-1,3]$
questions.worked_solution:
The graph of the function $f(x)=(x-1)^{2}-2$ can be obtained in the following way:

- Take the curve $y={x}^{2}.$

- Translate it by $1$ units to the right,  to get $y=(x-1)^{2}.$

- Finally, translate $y=(x-1)^{2}$  by $2$ units down to get $f(x)=(x-1)^{2}-2.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938271/assets/f53a4f97166877085c90acc01e3f8d0c6ac7bb3f704bbfb792d747122d314013.png)

A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test. 

- The function $f(x)$ is invertible on each of the intervals $x\in (-\infty ,1]$ and $x\in (1,\infty ).$ On these intervals, a horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938271/assets/b088c8ed1974a7c259dd54f85aec7a124579981971babfe8dee0313ca23b6458.png)

  

- The function $f(x)$ is not invertible on the interval $x\in (-1,3].$ On this interval, some horizontal lines will intersect the curve more than once.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938271/assets/b3af13782a01213bb09fdeef38fbeb3fbca3f41348036e6786b4efa74a0166b4.png)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and II only".

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938271/assets/def2afaad6d1f74ca3ac8833ed6e35efea1296b324ef5a14c2d9513983a63456.png)

Determine the largest interval on which the function $f(x)$ (shown above) is invertible.
questions.worked_solution:
First, notice that the domain of our function is $x\in [-2,4].$

A function is invertible on a particular interval if and only if it's a one-to-one function on that interval. To determine the intervals on which the function is invertible, we use the horizontal line test.

- The function $f(x)$ does not pass the horizontal line test on the interval $x\in [-2,0].$ In this case, the horizontal line $y=-2$ intersects the graph at more than one point.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938271/assets/033b9e827caf4fc89d4b179c769f5115254c811953f93caf33d0959bfd063235.png)

- The function $f(x)$ is invertible on the interval $x\in [0,4].$ On this interval, a horizontal line will intersect the curve at most once, no matter where we draw the line.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13938271/assets/4c91aa95131758065b1d8befe7c69895dc51d2f984a04cc8f06932a32e552792.png)

Therefore, the largest interval on which the function is invertible is:

$$
x\in [0,4]
$$
